app.title: mei-friend: browser editor for MEI music encodings
app.summary: A person opens a music encoding from a local file, a URL, a public repertoire list or a GitHub repository. The XML source and the engraved notation appear next to each other and stay linked. They fix the encoding by typing in the source or by selecting notes in the notation and pressing keys that insert, delete or change elements. Schema validation and an accidental checker point out problems as they go. They can line the encoding up against zones on the scanned source page and add editorial markup and annotations. When they are done, they download the corrected encoding as MEI, MIDI, SVG or PDF, or commit it back to the repository.

task.text: Clean up a music encoding that came from optical recognition or format conversion, checking it against its engraving and the source facsimile, and add editorial markup and annotations.

data.text: One structured XML encoding of a musical score, rendered as engraved notation and optionally linked to scanned page images through zones, kept in a git repository.
data.item: an element of the encoding, such as a note, chord, rest or control mark, that has an id and shows both in the source text and in the notation

stage.text: cleaning machine-generated music encodings after optical recognition or conversion, before publishing the edition

mechanism.text: A code editor with the XML and a notation pane with the engraving sit side by side. Selecting in either one highlights and scrolls to the same element in the other, and in the facsimile pane, where zones are drawn over the page image. Keyboard commands in the notation pane rewrite the encoding, which re-renders at once, while validation and checker panels list problems linked to lines.

field.text: music encoding and digital scholarly editing in digital musicology

workflow.name: correct a machine-generated structured encoding against its rendering and source

steps.here: Open MEI, MusicXML, Humdrum, ABC, PAE or lute tablature from a file, by drag and drop, from a URL or the public repertoire, or by cloning a GitHub repository through the server proxy.
The encoding is engraved page by page next to its XML. Clicking a note highlights its source line and its facsimile zone, and the arrow and page keys move through notes, measures and pages.

steps.step: find and fix problems in the item
steps.here: Single keys on selected notes add slurs, ties, dynamics, accidentals, clefs and beams, change pitch and duration, or delete elements. The source can also be edited directly, with tag matching, folding and schema-based autocomplete.

The RNG schema named in the file is loaded to validate the encoding, with errors marked in the gutter. A code checker lists accidental and meter-conformance problems, and each one can be fixed on its own or all at once.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: Selected notation is wrapped in editorial markup such as supplied, unclear, sic/corr, orig/reg, add/del or choice, each shown in its own colour. Annotations can be written inline or as stand-off Web Annotations, and are listed in the enrichment panel.

Download the encoding as MEI, MIDI, SVG or a PDF with a chosen page range, or commit to GitHub, which opens a branch and pull request if the commit would conflict, and optionally run GitHub Actions on the file.

distinctive: The source text and its rendered engraving are linked both ways at the element level by xml:id, so a click in either one finds the same note in the other and in the scanned page.
Single keystrokes on notes selected in the rendering insert or change notation elements (slurs, hairpins, accidentals, clef changes) and rewrite the XML underneath.
Validation uses the schema the file itself names, plus checks for this field: accidentals against the key signature, and staff durations against the time signature.
Editorial markup follows the scholarly-edition vocabulary (sic/corr, orig/reg, add/del, supplied, unclear, choice), and the person can switch which alternative reading is engraved.
Editing several people can work on together goes through git: a commit that would conflict is moved to a branch with a pull request, and Actions workflows can be run on the file.

parts.title: Encoding editor
parts.summary: A CodeMirror pane with the XML of the encoding, offering tag matching, folding, search, schema-based hints and wrapping a selection in a tag, so the person can fix the source by hand.

spans.first: // mapped to body under MAC OSX

parts.title: Notation panel
parts.summary: Shows the Verovio engraving of the encoding with paging and zoom. The person selects notes there and edits them with single-key commands, and the selection is highlighted in the source and the facsimile.

parts.title: Facsimile panel
parts.summary: Draws the zones of the encoding over the scanned source page. The person can resize, move, insert and delete zones, and clicking a zone selects the element linked to it.

parts.title: Schema validation and code checker
parts.summary: Reports schema errors in a status badge and a report, and lists accidental and meter-conformance problems, with a button to fix each one or all of them.

parts.title: Enrichment panel
parts.summary: Tools to wrap selected notation in editorial markup or to attach annotations (highlight, describe, link, identify), and a list of all markup and annotations that moves to each one when clicked.

parts.title: GitHub open, fork, commit and Actions
parts.summary: Logs in to GitHub and routes git and API traffic through a server proxy, so the person can open or fork a repository, commit changes (with a branch and pull request when there is a conflict) and run Actions workflows on the file.

parts.title: MIDI playback and status bar
parts.summary: Plays the encoding back as MIDI and highlights the notes being played, with a choice of expansion for repeats, plus a status bar and a progress bar.
